sources.title: CORE Econ, The Economy 1.0, Unit 1: The Capitalist Revolution
sources.authority: Official open textbook maintained by CORE Econ.
sources.relevance: Defines capitalism, GDP comparisons, specialization, technological change, and causal explanation used in the Economy bank.
sources.evidence_used: Concept coverage, boundary cases, and exercise styles were reviewed before writing original bilingual diagnostic prompts.
sources.transfer_limits: The bank questions are original adaptations rather than copied exercises; expert review is still required for semantic and cultural validity.

sources.title: CORE Econ, The Economy 1.0, Unit 2: Technology, Population, and Growth
sources.authority: Official open textbook maintained by CORE Econ.
sources.relevance: Covers models, production functions, marginal and average products, Malthusian dynamics, and growth mechanisms.
sources.evidence_used: Concept definitions and applied reasoning patterns informed original single-operation prompts.
sources.transfer_limits: Short diagnostic items cannot reproduce the unit's full historical argument or establish psychometric validity.

sources.title: CORE Econ, The Economy 1.0, Unit 3: Scarcity, Work, and Choice
sources.authority: Official open textbook maintained by CORE Econ.
sources.relevance: Covers feasible frontiers, marginal rates of transformation and substitution, constrained choice, and income/substitution effects.
sources.evidence_used: Diagrams and choice mechanisms were translated into self-contained verbal and numerical questions.
sources.transfer_limits: Text-only items simplify graphical reasoning and require later expert and participant validation.

sources.title: CORE Econ, The Economy 1.0, Unit 4: Social Interactions
sources.authority: Official open textbook maintained by CORE Econ.
sources.relevance: Covers strategic interaction, Nash equilibrium, public goods, social dilemmas, and social preferences.
sources.evidence_used: Game scenarios and equilibrium distinctions informed original atomic questions.
sources.transfer_limits: The prompts diagnose narrow concepts and do not replace full game-theoretic derivations or human review.
